name: Nordic national romanticism
summary: Painting that builds a nation's image from its own land, myths and home life: pale northern light, lake and forest, folk legend and the farm room. Painters trained in Paris bring back plein-air method and apply it to Nordic subjects.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture can give a young nation a face by painting its own land, light, legends and home with the best methods of Europe.
design_principles: Paint the northern landscape in a cool, pale key: a long horizon, a low sun and a sky that covers 40–60% of the height.
Use a clear, decorative outline on figures and legends: a contour of 2–4mm and flat or lightly modelled fields of colour.
Simplify the scene into 3 to 5 large shapes (lake, forest wall, sky, a figure) and tilt the space slightly flat.
Draw on national material: epic poem, folk costume, farm interiors, birch, spruce and granite.
Paint the interior as a bright, tidy, white-and-red room with natural window light and a pattern of folk textiles.
Keep the colour restrained and cool, with one warm accent in red ochre, a wooden building or a costume.
Combine plein-air observation with a symbolist or decorative arrangement: the scene is true, and the layout is designed.
anti_patterns: Tropical or Mediterranean colour and a warm golden sun
Classical gods, Roman ruins and Italianate scenery
Busy ornate frames of detail without a clear silhouette
Urban, industrial or cosmopolitan modern-life subjects
Sentimental detail that hides the simple structure of the land

composition.layout: Large, simple bands or masses: horizon at 40–60% of the height, a forest edge or lake shore as a decorative line, and the figures set as a frieze across the lower third.
composition.focal_point: A figure or a red building at 1/3 from the side, against the pale area of sky or water.
composition.format: Panoramic landscape at 3:2 to 2:1; a tall 1:2 format for legend and decorative panels.

principles.rule: Keep 30–50% of the picture as calm sky, lake or snow, with almost no detail.
Repeat trunk, wave or pattern shapes 6–15 times in a regular beat, with a small change of height and spacing.
Set cool blue, green and grey at about 75% of the area, and a warm red or ochre accent at 5–10%.
Use 3 planes: a dark foreground edge, a middle band of trees or figures, and a pale distance.
Hold the picture to one dominant colour key and vary the shapes inside it.

palette.strategy: A cool, light northern key of blue-grey, forest green and white, with one warm accent in red ochre and a touch of gold.
palette.distribution: Cool blues, greys and greens 60–70%, white and snow 15–20%, warm earth 10–15%, the red accent under 5%.
palette.ground: A pale grey or cream ground that keeps the picture light.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint, with tempera and watercolour for decorative and folk subjects.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Canvas, often large for public commission; paper for the watercolour sketch.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Broad, flat strokes of 10–30mm in sky and water, and a firm, drawn contour of 2–4mm on figures and trunks.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: Thin, matt layers with little impasto; the decorative pictures use flat, tempera-like fields.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Clear silhouette edges on figures and trunks against a soft sky; lost edges only in mist and snow.

light_and_modelling.light: Low, long northern light: a midsummer night glow or a diffuse winter day, with a long cast shadow.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Light modelling in 3–4 steps; the form reads as a clear shape against the sky more than as a volume.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Cool blue and violet shadows, with snow as a light-blue plane.
light_and_modelling.temperature: A cool overall key with a single warm window, timber wall or costume as the focal accent.

subject.typical: Lake and forest, birch and pine, mid-winter and midsummer, folk legend and the epic Kalevala, farm interiors, peasant costume.
subject.figure_scale: Figures take 15–40% of the height in landscape and 60–90% in the decorative panel.
subject.treatment: A calm, solemn or dreamy mood; the nation and its home are shown as lasting and dignified.

surface.finish: Matt, with a clear and dry surface.
surface.texture: Light canvas weave and visible broad strokes in the sky; flat and even in the decorative fields.

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). The Nationalmuseum (Stockholm) catalogue holds the central works; add its object ids in wave 2, once each licence is read.

emotion.target_response: Belonging and quiet pride: the viewer feels a home landscape that is old, calm and theirs.

use_cases: Nordic heritage and tourism art direction
book illustration for myth and legend
avoid_when: The brief asks for urban energy, glamour or a hot, saturated palette.
The subject comes from a culture other than the Nordic one, where the folk symbols would be borrowed.

modifiers.how: Keep the northern landscape and the cool key; drop the contour, break the sky and water into touches of 5–15mm, and raise the value of the shadows.
